newsitem.title: FRANCE: French watchdog sets Spie health warning.
newsitem.headline: French watchdog sets Spie health warning.

text.p: The French stock market regulator COB has posted a warning of financial risk to employees intending to take part in a buy-out of construction firm Spie Batignolles, a unit of electrical engineering firm Schneider.

Spie's financial projections presented in the buy-out offer rest on uncertain provisional data which depart from accounts which show a lack of, or mediocre, profitability, the COB said in a prominent notice on the subscription document.
The 100-franc ($18.27) subscription price is higher than Spie's attributable net asset value of 65.80 francs at the end of 1996.
Amec Plc is buying around 40 percent of Spie.

Amec has an option to buy Spie shares, which is exercisable at its own initiative and does not constitute a guarantee to buy. The exercise price has a ceiling and Amec can exercise its option after expert valuations on the price, the COB said.
It said indirect ownership of shares in Financiere Spie Batignolles implied a risk of illiquidity if Amec chose not to exercise its option to buy shares held by FCPE and FSB Investissement.
The floor price mechanism in the offer did not contitute a guarantee unless Amec exercised its option to buy, the COB said.
Spie managing fdirector Jean Monville told Reuters that the COB notice were in line with what the company itself had told its employees.

"We have already raised the points made by the COB. I do not think they will have any consequence," he said. "It is too early to say if the employee buy-out is going well but it is going ahead in an excellent climate."
Spie is offering employees a chance to buy 60 percent of the shares and Amec between 40 and 48.6 percent, depending on the level of employee take-up.
If Spie receives more than 180 million francs in employees' subscriptions it may use the surplus in a capital increase, Monville said.
